transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Suncrest Head of Platform), Ravi Menon (Suncrest CTO), Aisha Brown (Infra)

Summary: quick renewal check-in to align on contracted capacity uplift, EU region pilot timeline, and SOC/compliance handoffs. SE to run throughput bench, legal to confirm amendment, Redwood to send pricing for 12-month extension with staged provisioning.

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call — say hi?
00:06 Lena (Suncrest): Hi, Lena here. Thanks.
00:08 Ravi (Suncrest): Ravi — CTO.
00:10 Aisha (Suncrest): Aisha on infra.
00:12 Jordan (Redwood SE): Jordan from Redwood.
00:14 Maya (Redwood AE): Cool. Agenda — capacity bump request, EU staging plan, and timeline for contract extension. We have about 45 minutes.

02:03 Lena: To set context, our usage has spiked 30% last quarter, lots more chat sessions. We're hitting our current committed pool and seeing queued requests during peak at 3pm our time. We're looking at additional reserved QPS plus bringing EU online.
02:41 Ravi: Also, we have a hard compliance kickoff in July — need SOC2 artifacts and the V P C deployment plan for legal.
03:02 Jordan: Understood. For the capacity uplift are you thinking steady ramp or a jump? I remember you mentioned staged provisioning in your notes.
03:18 Lena: Staged. We want a 2-phase: immediate 20% uplift to remove queuing, then +40% over next three months as we onboard new product flows.
03:33 Maya: Sounds reasonable. For the immediate uplift we can do reserved capacity top-up on Dedicated, or if you prefer lower commit we can add burst delta on Hosted while you confirm long-term numbers. Tradeoff is cost predictability vs. lower up-front commitment.
03:57 Ravi: We prefer predictable latency and isolation — leaning toward Dedicated. But we want to keep cost tight. Can you lay out economics for both?
04:18 Maya: Sure — I'll include both in the pricing sheet. Dedicated shows lower per-token cost at higher commit; Hosted burst has higher unit cost but zero infra ops. We'll include a staged commitment with a 12-month amendment option.

06:05 Aisha: Quick technical Q — is KV cache and prefix caching preserved across autoscale? We saw some cold starts last week and KV cold misses caused hits in latency.
06:22 Jordan: Right — good question. Our runtime keeps a per-instance KV cache; during autoscale we warm caches using a prefetch policy for your common prefixes. There can be a short tail of cold misses during big scale events; we've seen that on some workloads where sequence length and prompt distribution changes rapidly.
06:46 Aisha: Is there an option for persistent KW — I mean KV — to reduce those misses?
06:52 Jordan: Persistent KV across instances is on the roadmap but not generally available. For now the recommended pattern is to pin a small pool of warm instances and configure autoscale thresholds to prefer scale-up before scale-out for short bursts; that reduces cache churn. Also we can suggest a small dedicated warm pool as part of the staging plan.
07:20 Aisha: Okay, that'll help.

08:05 Lena: Compliance — we need KMS integration and audit logs in the private deployment. Our legal asked for encryption at rest for model cache and token logs.
08:19 Jordan: KMS/HSM integrations are supported in Redwood Private; we can integrate your KMS and provide per-request envelope encryption. Audit logs are in the Console — we can increase retention for the enterprise pack. We'll attach the SOC2 and ISO artifacts in the security packet.
08:38 Ravi: When you say "Private", are we talking fully on-prem or V P C in our cloud? We prefer VPC with customer-managed keys.
08:45 Maya: VPC is the recommended path for you — Redwood Private with a customer VPC peering and KMS access. On-prem requires a heavier deployment but it's optional. We'll clarify the network topology in the runbook.

10:12 Maya: Quick note on region onboarding — EU pilot: Jordan, can you run throughput bench against the eu-west endpoints with their traffic profile?
10:22 Jordan: Yep. We'll need a snapshot of current traffic: p50/p95 token lengths, concurrency, and sample prompt shapes. Aisha, can you share that?
10:30 Aisha: Yes, I can export the Profile from our gateway logs and redacted prompts. Expect that by EOD Tuesday.
10:36 Jordan: Great. Bench will test token throughput and tail latencies; we'll run both quantized model variants and full FP16 to show the tradeoffs. We'll also test batching and cache behaviors.

12:05 Lena: Important — our product team will only accept MLP when p95 is under 300ms for short completions (<120 tokens). Is that feasible across EU?
12:20 Jordan: That depends on the model family and instance type. On dedicated A100-like hardware we can generally hit p95s around 200–250ms for <120 tokens with optimized kernels and tight batching. On cheaper instances or with heavy batching you could see higher p95s. We'll surface a latency/cost matrix.
12:43 Ravi: Also need to confirm fallback behavior — if EU capacity is saturated, traffic should failover to US but with graceful degradation and notify.
12:56 Maya: Smart routing policy can do region failover. We'll propose a routing config: primary EU, fallback US-hosted less-capacity variant with lower-cost model, plus alerting. That will be in the playbook.

15:00 Aisha: One more infra detail — how long to provision new dedicated pool? We need to schedule the rollout to avoid product launch conflicts.
15:10 Maya: Typical lead time is 5–10 business days for dedicated GPU pool provisioning depending on region capacity and current backlog; we'll add a prioritized queue for you. For staged rollout EU pilot should be possible in two weeks if you sign the amendment this month.
15:28 Lena: Two weeks is fine. Legal needs the amendment text; what are the key commercial terms?
15:34 Maya: We'll include term length (12 months default), staged capacity milestones, price per reserved unit, and an exit clause for scale-down at the 6-month checkpoint. Also SLA targets and incident credits.
15:49 Ravi: SLA details — what's typical p99 latency guarantee?
15:52 Jordan: SLA focuses on availability and latency SLOs for token streaming; p99 is tricky given model variance, but we do provide incident-based credits if the runtime can't meet agreed SLOs. We'll include a sample SLA doc.

18:10 Speaker 1: (inaudible)
18:30 Jordan: I'll include an appendix on quantization recommendations — 4-bit/8-bit variants often give 1.6–2× throughput with minimal quality regression for many flows, but this is workload dependent. Our Optimize team can run a quick eval.
18:57 Lena: We're worried about hallucination/regression if you quantize; product will want a roll-back path.
19:05 Jordan: Absolutely. Our rollout tooling supports canary and A/B tests, automatic rollback on quality regression thresholds tied to your eval sets. We'll store evals in the Console and alert on drift.

21:10 Maya: Recap next steps: I'll send pricing and the 12-month amendment draft; Jordan will run the bench once we get traffic profile; Aisha to send logs. Legal will loop in and confirm timeline.
21:30 Aisha: I'll get logs to Jordan by Tuesday.
21:36 Lena: Expect legal to review within 5 business days after you send the amendment.
21:42 Maya: Great. Any other blockers?
21:47 Ravi: One tiny thing — ModelCloud reached out offering a cheaper burst model; curious what your differentiation is beyond price.
22:01 Maya: Two main differences — production-grade routing/observability (token-level cost + tracing) and unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private. Also we have the Optimize playbook for quantization and cache tuning to reduce unit cost. We'll include a short comparison note.
22:20 Lena: Good.

24:05 Jordan: A note for the bench — to get realistic numbers please include concurrent customer-facing sessions and internal batch jobs, otherwise numbers will be optimistic.
24:20 Aisha: Will do.

26:40 Maya: Last thing — do we want a 30-minute executive sync after the benchmark to review results and finalize amendment?
26:48 Lena: Yes please, schedule for the week after 6/22.
26:52 Maya: I'll coordinate calendar invites.

29:00 Closing: thanks all.

Action recap (verbatim): Maya to send pricing and amendment (due 6/14), Jordan to prep bench and run EU throughput tests (week of 6/22), Aisha to share traffic profile (due 6/16), Lena to confirm regions and compliance contacts (due 6/18).

Links shared on call: pricing template (drive link), security packet (s3://redwood-security/suncrest-soc2.zip), bench playbook (docs.redwood/internal/bench-playbook).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attribution, some technical terms transcribed as letters (e.g., V P C, K V cache).
